note: Independent scoped source rejudgment after the raw CircuitID API adaptation. RFC 1195 Section 4.4 states: 'All IS-IS routers are therefore required to transmit and receive ISO 9542 ISH packets on point-to-point links.' TestRFC1195ISHTransmitReceive drives a configured P2P circuit, requires an ISH addressed to AllESs before the IIH, decodes its configured NET and IPv4 capability, dispatches a valid peer ISH through production handling, and requires one initializing IPv4 adjacency without bypassing the subsequent three-way handshake. TestRFC1195ISHVethTransport uses the actual AF_PACKET transport at both ends of an isolated veth pair, sends the encoded ISH through SendISH, filters the peer ifindex, requires exact AllESs destination and PDU bytes, and decodes the NET and holding time. Its sole edit discards CircuitInfo's added identity result; all inputs and assertions remain unchanged. Removing SendISH, corrupting its delivery, or removing P2P receive processing would fail those assertions. TestRFC1195ISHRejectsCorruptionAndWrongCircuit rejects corrupted P2P discovery and discovery on broadcast circuits. TestRFC1195ISHConfiguredPassword and TestRFC1195ISHWrongPassword retain the configured per-link-password send/receive and missing/wrong-password controls. TestRFC1195NeighborWithoutISHStillFormsAdjacency is supplementary IIH-only interoperability coverage, not the refusal proof for the mandatory transmit/receive capability. No claim or requirement scope changed. The tuple edit originally staled the veth unit's observation. ROOT then re-recorded that positive through the official revert route: the named unit passed its clean run and failed after SendISH was disabled through an overlay, with no skip; both VMs stopped. The reviewer read job-isis-raw-identity-rfc1195-own-kernel-record-157545f6.log and the native updated discrimination record. Both runs used Ze's own runtime system, module release 7.3.0-ze and kernel SHA256 e3b00fe91d5ce09cd4133f4d455e9295e815df9da6aac25a4039befa8a41caec. This fresh observation proves the tagged veth transport claim's dependence on SendISH, not additional protocol or whole-RFC conformance.
